summary: You have a clear mission concept, with a well-supported case for a single satellite and a sensible report structure, and your STK evidence gives the design a solid base. The main gaps are an unresolved launch vehicle choice, unexplained orbital elements, an incomplete end-of-life analysis, and several broken or unfinished sentences and references. Fixing these would move the report up a band.
next_steps: Resolve the launch vehicle: choose one option, justify it against your target orbit, and remove the conflicting Vega E and piggyback statements. Check the 2024 first-flight claim against a source.

Explain your orbital elements in the text: why the inclination gives retrograde motion, what sun-synchronous means here, and how the RAAN of 27.33° was chosen. Make the argument of latitude consistent between text and table.

Complete the end-of-life section: finish the drag-sail sentence, calculate the delta-v for any manoeuvre you propose, and replace the Wikipedia source with an approved reference. Also fix the duplicate rows 14 and 15 in the access table and attach your STK files.

criteria.C1: You clearly state the primary mission, the reason it is needed and why one spacecraft is used, supported by cited literature on coral reef monitoring. To reach the top band, name the operator and customers separately and explain each role. Give more specific detail on who would use the data and how.
criteria.C2: Your STK screenshots and access table show a solid design process. To reach the top band, the design must be consistent and fully justified. Explain the launch site and vehicle choice in terms of your target inclination, justify the orbit and its elements, and check your ground station contact times against an elevation mask. Complete the manoeuvre and end-of-life analysis with calculated delta-v and attach the software files.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion summarises the mission segments and identifies the launch risk and alternatives, which is useful. To reach the top band, draw specific conclusions from your evidence. Refer to the access durations, contact times and perturbation results, and state what they mean for the mission's feasibility.
criteria.C4: The report has clear headings and a logical structure. To improve, finish the unfinished sentences and fix the broken reference [10]. Use approved sources instead of Wikipedia. Number and title every figure and table, and check the contents page against the section headings. Proofread for grammar and keep the language formal throughout.
